items.title: Tesla raises capex plan to $25 billion for AI push

featured_image.name: Elon Musk's plan to redesign the world's factories... and perhaps the  planet too: humanoid robots that work 12 hours a day, never rest, and use  artificial intelligence

items.description: Tesla will spend more than $25 billion on capital expenditures this year, roughly tripling last year's outlay, as the electric vehicle maker accelerates its pivot towards artificial intelligence and robotics amid a slowing car business.

items.title: Nuclear leaders convene in Busan, framing reactors as AI-era infrastructure

featured_image.name: Nuclear Leaders Highlight Power Needs for AI Era

items.description: As the world prepares to mark the 40th anniversary of the Chernobyl disaster on April 26, the nuclear power industry finds itself in the midst of a striking resurgence. Driven by surging electricity demand from artificial intelligence, climate targets, and fresh government commitments, roughly 75 reactors are now under construction worldwide and about 120 more are planned, according to the World Nuclear Association.[1][2]

items.title: Asian shares retreat from record highs as oil tops $103 on Iran tensions

featured_image.name: Asian stock markets plunge amid Trump's ultimatum on Iran

items.description: Asian markets pulled back on Thursday after briefly touching record highs, as rising oil prices and uncertainty over the U.S.-Iran conflict prompted investors to lock in profits from a weeks-long technology-driven rally.

items.title: IDF removes 40 Israeli settlers who crossed into Syria

featured_image.name: Israeli troops remove Israeli settler group who crossed into ...

items.description:
Around 40 Israeli settler activists from the far-right Pioneers of Bashan organization crossed into Syrian territory on Wednesday, barricading themselves on a rooftop on the outskirts of the Druze village of Hader at the foot of Mount Hermon and demanding the Israeli government approve Jewish settlements in Syria.[1][2][3]

The Israeli military said the group gathered near the northern border before advancing several hundred meters — roughly half a kilometer — into Syria. IDF troops escorted the activists back to Israeli territory and handed them over to police.[2][1]

"The IDF strongly condemns this incident and emphasizes its severity, which constitutes a criminal offense that endangers civilians and IDF troops," the military said.[1][2]

items.title: White House says Iran ship seizures don't breach ceasefire

featured_image.name: Trump extends ceasefire, offering time for Tehran to unify around ...

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps seized two commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, hours after President Donald Trump announced an open-ended extension of the U.S.-Iran ceasefire. The White House moved swiftly to minimize the incident, insisting it did not constitute a violation of the truce.

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills journalist in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon kill Lebanese journalist ...

items.description:
Lebanese journalist Amal Khalil was killed on Wednesday in an Israeli airstrike in the southern village of al-Tiri, prompting Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam to accuse Israel of committing war crimes against media workers. Khalil, 43, a reporter for the daily newspaper Al-Akhbar, had been covering renewed hostilities in southern Lebanon when she was struck and buried under rubble for hours before her body could be recovered.[1][2]

Khalil and freelance photographer Zeinab Faraj were reporting near al-Tiri when an Israeli strike hit a vehicle in front of them. The two journalists ran into a nearby house for cover, which was then also hit by an Israeli strike, according to Lebanon's health ministry and military officials. Faraj sustained a head injury and was evacuated to Tibnin Hospital, where she underwent surgery and is in stable condition. Khalil was trapped beneath the rubble for roughly six hours before rescuers retrieved her body.[3][4][5][1]

items.title: Pope Leo visits notorious Equatorial Guinea prison on Africa tour

featured_image.name: Secretive deal leaves deportees from the US stuck in Equatorial ...

items.description: Pope Leo XIV visited one of Equatorial Guinea's most notorious correctional facilities on Wednesday, delivering a message of hope to inmates at Bata Prison while drawing attention to the country's long-documented human rights abuses — particularly as the facility has come under renewed scrutiny following U.S. deportations of third-country migrants to the Central African nation.

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills 5 near mosque in northern Gaza

featured_image.name: Israeli airstrike kills 5 Palestinians in Rafah, southern Gaza

items.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck a group of civilians near the Al-Qassam Mosque in Beit Lahia, northern Gaza, on Wednesday night, killing five Palestinians including three children, according to Gaza's civil defense agency.[1][2][3]

"Five Palestinians, including three children, were killed in an Israeli airstrike that targeted a group of civilians near Al-Qassam mosque in Beit Lahia," the agency said in a statement carried by AFP. The bodies were transported to Al-Shifa hospital in Gaza City, which confirmed receiving them. The civil defense did not specify the ages of the children killed. The Israeli military told AFP it was checking the reports.[1]

items.title: Google and OpenAI launch rival AI agent platforms on the same day

featured_image.name: Introducing Google Workspace Studio: Build AI Agents to Automate Work, No  Coding Required

items.description: The race to define the future of work entered a new phase this week as Google and OpenAI both unveiled AI agent platforms designed to automate office tasks, setting up a direct clash over who will control the next layer of enterprise productivity software.

items.title: Iran denies Trump's claim he stopped execution of eight women

featured_image.name: Iran agrees not to execute eight women tied to anti-regime protests after  Trump's public appeal

items.description: Iran's judiciary flatly rejected President Donald Trump's assertion that he had intervened to stop the execution of eight women protesters, calling the claim "fake news" and saying the president had been "misled" — setting up a sharp public dispute between Washington and Tehran even as nuclear negotiations continue.

items.title: US military seizes three Iranian oil tankers in Asian waters

featured_image.name: US forces interdict another fugitive tanker ship in Indian Ocean

items.description:
The U.S. military intercepted at least three Iranian-flagged oil tankers in Asian waters on Wednesday, redirecting them away from positions near India, Malaysia, and Sri Lanka as Washington extends the enforcement of its naval blockade well beyond the Strait of Hormuz, according to a Reuters exclusive citing shipping and security sources.[1][2]

The vessels include the supertanker Dorena, fully loaded with roughly 2 million barrels of crude oil and last tracked off the Indian coast, the Deep Sea supertanker, and the smaller tanker Sevin. U.S. Central Command confirmed on Wednesday that the Dorena is under escort by a U.S. Navy destroyer in the Indian Ocean after it attempted to "violate the blockade," and said the total number of vessels directed to turn around or return to port had risen to 29 since the blockade began on April 13.[3][4][5][6][1]

items.title: UK to pay France £660M in new deal to curb Channel crossings

featured_image.name: UK Links France's Border Plan Funding to Performance in New ...

items.description:
The United Kingdom has agreed to pay France roughly £660 million over three years in a new deal to curb illegal small boat crossings of the English Channel, with Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set to formally sign the agreement on Thursday, according to the Guardian.[1]

The deal, which will run until March 2029, comes after weeks of fraught negotiations that saw the previous £478 million arrangement expire on March 31 and required a £16.2 million emergency two-month extension to keep patrols running while talks continued.[2][3]

items.title: Study finds early solar system solids formed in days, not millennia

featured_image.name: Meteorites : Macro photo of chondrites

items.description: The first solid materials in our solar system condensed far more quickly than traditional models predicted, forming through a process of non-equilibrium condensation in a dynamic and thermally chaotic protoplanetary disk, according to a study published in Nature on April 22.[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky distances himself from 'Donnyland' Donbas proposal, pushes to restart talks

featured_image.name: Ukraine proposes creating 'Donnyland' to satisfy Trump - Yahoo

items.description:
President Volodymyr Zelensky pushed back on Wednesday against a reported proposal by Ukrainian negotiators to rename a contested strip of the Donbas region "Donnyland" — a portmanteau of Donetsk, Donald, and Disneyland — as a diplomatic gesture aimed at winning the favor of U.S. President Donald Trump.

"The main thing is that Donetsk Oblast and Luhansk Oblast remain Ukraine — as long as it's not 'Putinland.' That is the most important thing," Zelensky told reporters on April 22, according to the Kyiv Independent. He added that in negotiations he uses "no other terms than Donetsk Oblast, Luhansk Oblast, our Donbas, and the territory of Ukraine."[1]

items.title: Pentagon says clearing Hormuz mines could take 6 months

featured_image.name: Navy mine-clearing ships depart Asia as Strait of Hormuz ...

items.description: The Pentagon has informed Congress that fully clearing Iranian sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz could take up to six months, and that the operation is unlikely to be completed before the war with Iran ends, according to a Washington Post exclusive report published Wednesday. The assessment, delivered during a classified briefing for members of the House Armed Services Committee on April 21, paints a far grimmer picture of the mine threat than the optimistic tone struck by President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in recent weeks.[1][2][3][4]

featured_image.name: Trump pulls back on Iran threats after warning a ...

items.description: President Donald Trump declared on Tuesday that Iran is "collapsing financially" and losing $500 million a day, escalating his rhetoric as a fragile ceasefire teeters and diplomatic efforts to end the nearly two-month-old conflict stall.

items.title: Iran seizes two ships, fires on third in Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Iran fires on, seizes two container ships near Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps opened fire on three commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, seizing two and leaving a third stranded along the Iranian coast, in a sharp escalation that came just hours after President Trump announced he was indefinitely extending a ceasefire with Tehran.

The IRGC captured the Panama-flagged MSC Francesca and the Liberia-flagged Epaminondas, both container ships, and directed them to Iranian waters, according to a statement carried by AFP. A third vessel, the Greek-owned Euphoria, was also targeted and is now stranded off the Iranian coast, according to semiofficial Iranian news agency Fars. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency reported that the first ship was "assaulted by a gunboat" from the IRGC at approximately 7:55 a.m. local time.[1][2][3][4][5]

The IRGC claimed the vessels "allegedly operated without authorization, repeatedly violated regulations, manipulated navigational aid systems and sought to covertly exit the Strait of Hormuz, endangering maritime security". The statement added that "disruption of order and safety in the Strait of Hormuz is our red line".[6][1]

items.description: Google Cloud opened its annual Next conference in Las Vegas on Wednesday with a sweeping set of announcements centered on Gemini Enterprise, the company's agentic AI platform, while deepening partnerships with consulting giants Accenture and BCG to accelerate adoption across global enterprises.
